relations.note: Picus is Saturn’s son and transmits his lineage to Faunus.
A rationalizing antiquarian genealogy makes the culture hero Sterces Picus’s father.
Virgil calls Circe Picus’s coniunx, possibly meaning his actual wife.

relations.myth: Circe transforms Picus into a bird
relations.note: Circe strikes Picus with her golden wand and drugs, making him a bird.

relations.myth: Circe propositions Picus during a boar hunt
relations.note: Circe proposes sexual union, but Picus rejects her out of fidelity to Canens.

relations.myth: Circe punishes Picus for rejecting her
relations.note: After Picus refuses her, Circe transforms him into a woodpecker.
Picus is Canens’s faithful husband; his disappearance causes her fatal wandering.
Janus is Picus’s father-in-law through Picus’s marriage to Canens.
Picus fathers Faunus in the stable Latin royal genealogy.
They drink together, are bound by Numa, and jointly help summon Jupiter.

relations.myth: Egeria reveals how Numa can capture Picus
relations.note: Egeria identifies Picus’s ritual knowledge and teaches Numa how to compel him.

relations.myth: Picus helps draw Jupiter from heaven
relations.note: Picus and Faunus help summon Jupiter while acknowledging his superior control over lightning.

relations.myth: Mars’s woodpecker guides the Picentine settlers
relations.note: The woodpecker associated with Picus is sacred to Mars, without secure identity or parentage.
Servius preserves a disputed variant in which Picus loves or marries Pomona.

relations.myth: Circe offers Sol as Picus’s father-in-law
relations.note: Circe proposes that Picus marry her and receive Sol as his father-in-law.

relations.myth: Circe invokes Hecate after transforming Picus
relations.note: Circe invokes Hecate while changing Picus’s companions after Picus becomes a bird.

relations.myth: Circe invokes Night after transforming Picus
relations.note: Circe invokes Night while changing Picus’s companions after Picus becomes a bird.

relations.myth: Circe invokes Erebus after transforming Picus
relations.note: Circe invokes Erebus while changing Picus’s companions after Picus becomes a bird.

relations.myth: Circe invokes Chaos after transforming Picus
relations.note: Circe invokes Chaos while changing Picus’s companions after Picus becomes a bird.
Ancient antiquarian and theological traditions conflate Picus with Picumnus, though modern scholarship distinguishes them.
Chronographic traditions recast Picus as Zeus Picus, a universal primeval king.
